def: a mistake in a program that stops it working correctly
ex: Users reported a bug when they try to log in.

def: a part of a program that does something useful for the user
ex: The new version adds a dark mode feature.

def: the instructions, written by a programmer, that tell a computer what to do
ex: She writes clean, easy-to-read code.

def: to find and remove the errors in a program
ex: I spent the afternoon debugging the payment page.

def: a computer that stores data and sends it to other computers over a network
ex: The website is slow because the server is overloaded.

def: an organised collection of information stored in a computer
ex: All the user accounts are kept in a database.

def: a request for information from a database
ex: This query returns all the orders from last month.

def: the part of a website or app that the user sees and interacts with
ex: He works on the frontend, mostly forms and buttons.

def: the part of a system that users do not see, where data is stored and processed
ex: The backend checks your password before letting you in.

def: a place where all the code of a project is stored and its changes are tracked
ex: Push your changes to the shared repository.

def: a saved set of changes to the code, with a short message describing it
ex: Each commit should do one clear thing.

def: (of a program or computer) to stop working suddenly
ex: The app crashes when you open a very large file.

def: the act of putting a new version of software into use
ex: The deployment failed because of a wrong setting.

def: a set of rules that lets two programs exchange data with each other
ex: The mobile app gets its data from our API.

def: a spare copy of data kept in case the original is lost
ex: The database backup runs every night.

def: a set of steps that a computer follows to solve a problem
ex: The search algorithm sorts the results by date.

def: a collection of data used for analysis or to train a model
ex: We trained the model on a dataset of 10,000 images.

def: a way of making computers learn from data instead of being given every rule
ex: Machine learning is used to filter spam email.

def: (of software) with code that anyone can read, use and change for free
ex: We use several open source libraries in this project.

def: code that automatically checks whether other code works correctly
ex: Write a test before you fix the bug.

def: a request for others to review and merge your code changes into the main branch
ex: Open a pull request when your feature is ready.

def: a clash that happens when two branches change the same lines of code
ex: I spent an hour resolving a merge conflict in the config.

def: to move a branch's commits on top of another branch to keep the history tidy
ex: Rebase your branch onto main before you merge.

def: to undo an earlier commit by applying the opposite change
ex: We reverted the commit that broke the build.

def: a return to a previous working version after a bad change
ex: The failed deploy triggered an automatic rollback.

def: to make a local copy of a remote repository
ex: Clone the repo and run the setup script.

def: a personal copy of someone else's repository that you can change freely
ex: I forked the project to fix a typo in the docs.

def: a file that lists what changed in each version
ex: Add a line to the changelog for every release.

def: the step where another developer reads your code before it is merged
ex: Her code review caught a security bug.

def: a test environment that copies production and is used just before release
ex: It works on staging but fails in production.

def: an automated series of steps that builds, tests and deploys code
ex: The pipeline runs the whole test suite on every push.

def: a lightweight package that holds an app and everything it needs to run
ex: Each service runs in its own container.

def: the gradual release of a change to more and more users
ex: We did a slow rollout to 5% of users first.

def: a period when a system is not available
ex: The upgrade caused ten minutes of downtime.

def: the proportion of time a system stays available
ex: Our servers have 99.9% uptime.

def: the delay between a request and its response
ex: Users far from the server see higher latency.

def: the amount of work a system handles in a given time
ex: The queue's throughput dropped after the update.

def: a component that spreads incoming traffic across several servers
ex: The load balancer sends you to the nearest server.

def: how well a system copes with a growing amount of work
ex: We picked this database for its scalability.

def: a period when a service stops working
ex: A cloud outage took down half the internet.

def: watching a system's health and performance over time
ex: Monitoring alerted us before users noticed.

def: recording what a program does so problems can be traced later
ex: Add some logging around the payment step.

def: a setup where code runs, such as development, staging or production
ex: This bug only shows up in the production environment.

def: setting up the servers and resources an app needs
ex: Provisioning a new server now takes minutes, not days.

def: a test that checks one small piece of code on its own
ex: Every function should have at least one unit test.

def: a test that checks that several parts work together
ex: The integration test runs against a real database.

def: a bug that brings back a problem that was already fixed
ex: The update introduced a regression in search.

def: a fake version of a component used to isolate a test
ex: We mock the API so the tests run offline.

def: an unusual situation at the edge of what the code expects
ex: Empty input is an edge case we forgot to handle.

def: a test that passes and fails at random without any code change
ex: A flaky test is worse than no test at all.

def: how much of the code is exercised by the tests
ex: Test coverage dropped below 70% this week.

def: a single URL that an API exposes for a specific action
ex: The login endpoint returns a token.

def: the actual data carried inside a request or message
ex: Send the user id in the request payload.

def: code that runs between a request and the final handler
ex: The auth middleware checks every request.

def: an external piece of code that your project needs to work
ex: Updating one dependency broke three others.

def: the period when a program is running, or the software that runs it
ex: The error only appears at runtime, never at compile time.

def: a program that turns source code into a form the computer can run
ex: The compiler flags the type error before you run anything.

def: to rewrite code so it is cleaner without changing what it does
ex: Let's refactor this file before we add more features.

def: old code that is still in use and hard to change safely
ex: Nobody on the team wants to touch the legacy code.

def: the future cost of choosing a quick solution over a solid one
ex: We're paying down technical debt this sprint.

def: standard code that has to be written the same way every time
ex: The framework removes a lot of boilerplate.

def: several tasks making progress at overlapping times
ex: The bug only appears under high concurrency.

def: a bug where the result depends on the exact timing of events
ex: Two threads wrote at the same time — a classic race condition.

def: a fault where a program keeps memory it no longer needs
ex: The memory leak crashed the server after about a day.

def: keeping a copy of data so it can be served faster next time
ex: Caching cut the page load time in half.

def: a cap on how many requests you can make in a period of time
ex: You hit the API's rate limit — wait a minute and retry.

def: deliberately slowing down requests to protect a system
ex: The service starts throttling clients under heavy load.

def: the structure that defines how data is organised in a database
ex: The migration changes the users table schema.

def: a script that changes the database structure in a controlled way
ex: Run the migrations after you pull the latest code.

def: a group of database changes that all succeed or all fail together
ex: Wrap both updates in a single database transaction.

def: keeping copies of data on several servers in sync
ex: Read queries are served from a replication follower.

def: checking that users are who they say they are
ex: We added two-factor authentication last month.

def: deciding what an authenticated user is allowed to do
ex: Authentication passed but authorization failed.

def: a string that proves a user is logged in, sent with each request
ex: The token expires one hour after you log in.

def: the period a user stays logged in, tracked by the server
ex: Closing the browser tab ended the session.

def: an automatic message a service sends to a URL when an event happens
ex: GitHub fires a webhook on every push.

def: a weakness in software that an attacker could take advantage of
ex: The scanner found a vulnerability in an old library.

def: turning data into a coded form that only authorised people can read
ex: All traffic between the apps uses end-to-end encryption.

def: an attack that slips malicious database commands into an input field
ex: Escaping user input prevents SQL injection.

def: a short fixed period in which a team completes a planned set of work
ex: This feature is scheduled for the next sprint.

def: a short daily meeting where the team shares progress and blockers
ex: Mention that blocker at standup tomorrow.

def: a meeting to review how the last sprint went and what to improve
ex: The retrospective raised the flaky tests again.

def: a high-level plan of what will be built and roughly when
ex: Dark mode is on the roadmap for next quarter.

def: the text you give an AI model to tell it what you want
ex: A clearer prompt gave a much better answer.

def: the step where a trained model produces an output for new input
ex: Inference runs on the GPU to keep it fast.

def: extra training that adapts a general model to a specific task
ex: Fine-tuning on our own tickets improved the classifier.

def: a list of numbers that represents the meaning of text or an image
ex: We store the embeddings in a vector database.

def: when a model learns the training data too closely and fails on new data
ex: The gap between train and test accuracy points to overfitting.
